Lancet 2025; published online Oct 29. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01919-1 (this is the suggested citation in every xlsx). Full record via doi.org: The Lancet 406(10521), 2804-2857.

sources.url_check: Fetched the explore-our-data HTML and extracted 30 or more direct xlsx links. Downloaded 1.1.5 in memory: 137 KB zip (PK header). DATA GUIDANCE says 'Indicator 1.1.5: Heat Related Mortality', authors Ballester, Basagaña, Ruiz-Cabrejos. The Global sheet has Year/AF/AN, with 2021 AN=558304. In 1.1.3 PWHL the Global sheet column TotalSunAgCon for 2024 is 639,855,005.65 (thousand hours). In 1.1.1 Attributable, 2024 Observed=30.79 days and Attributable_to_CC=25.75. 2.3.3 key finding: 156.7 million people living less than 1 m above sea level in 2024. use-our-data page confirms CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Note: lancetcountdown.org/data-platform/ returned 404; the working page is /explore-our-data/.
sources.site_use: Core source for 'Health consequences'. Charts: heat deaths 1990-2021 (global, then WHO region, then HDI group); work hours lost by sector and country 1990-2024; heatwave days per person, observed vs. without climate change (a clear attribution visual); wildfire smoke exposure days; people living less than 1 m above sea level. Drill-down goes global, then region, then country. Because of ShareAlike, CSV exports of these numbers must carry CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the citation.
sources.caveats: Heat mortality is modelled (DLNM meta-regression; exposure-response is meta-predicted for countries with no local studies) and stops at 2021. Indicator methods change between report years, so do not splice 2024-report and 2025-report vintages. Store the vintage with every number. The ShareAlike term propagates to our derived CSVs. The NC term is fine because the site is non-commercial, but it must stay that way. File names carry '-1'/'_v2' suffixes and will change for the 2026 vintage.

The ToS ban on bulk or automated download conflicts with a scripted pipeline unless permission is granted.

sources.publisher: Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED), UCLouvain
sources.measures: Event-level disasters (at least 10 deaths, at least 100 affected, an emergency declaration, or an appeal for international aid): deaths, injured, affected, homeless, damage (US$ thousands, adjusted), by hazard type, country and date
sources.coverage: Global, country and event level, 1900-present (reliable mainly from 2000)
sources.latest_release: Continuously updated. OWID's copy notes 'disasters reported up to April 2026' (EM-DAT datePublished 2026-04-28). FAIR archive: 2024 EM-DAT archive on UCLouvain Dataverse.

sources.format: XLSX export from the authenticated portal; archive on Dataverse
sources.license: Custom terms (https://doc.emdat.be/docs/legal/terms-of-use/), free for academic, non-profit, public-organisation and media use 'for research, teaching or information purposes'. Prohibited: 'Reproduce, copy, communicate, lend, or otherwise distribute EM-DAT or a substantial part of EM-DAT'; 'Create substitute or derivative databases of EM-DAT'; 'Share, use or transmit any portion of EM-DAT via the Internet to unauthorized users'; commercial use needs a paid Database License Agreement. Proper citation is mandatory. The FAIR archive is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
sources.citation: Emergency Events Database (EM-DAT), UCLouvain / CRED, Brussels, Belgium, accessed on YYYY-MM-DD, https://www.emdat.be/ (format from the EM-DAT Attribution and Citation Policy, 2025). Descriptor: Delforge, D., Wathelet, V., Below, R., Sofia, C. L., Tonnelier, M., van Loenhout, J. A. F., & Speybroeck, N. (2025). EM-DAT: the Emergency Events Database. International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction, 124, 105509.
sources.url_check: Fetched emdat.be (open access for non-commercial use). curl of doc.emdat.be terms-of-use extracted the verbatim prohibitions quoted. Citation-policy page fetched ('UCLouvain 2025'). public.emdat.be returned 200 and shows Login/Register, i.e. export is gated. The FAIR news page confirms the Dataverse DOI and the CC BY-NC-ND licence. doi.org resolved the Delforge 2025 descriptor.
sources.site_use: Global multi-hazard deaths and affected people: show only aggregated, charted values (e.g. deaths by hazard type by decade, global or continent), with the proper citation and a link out. Do NOT offer event-level or substantial CSV downloads, and do not cache a mirror of EM-DAT in our public R2 bucket. Email CRED (regina.below@uclouvain.be is named in the terms) for written permission to publish aggregate CSVs.
sources.caveats: Strong reporting bias: event counts rise mostly because reporting improved (OWID's subtitle warns about this). Heat deaths are badly under-recorded outside Europe. Economic damage is missing for most events. Includes non-climate hazards (earthquakes, volcanoes), which must be filtered out. Registration gating breaks a fully automated, reproducible pipeline.

Use OWID's EM-DAT aggregates only as a cross-check; licensing stays EM-DAT's. On processing: for GWIS it is 'minor' (regional sums of GWIS country values), so values equal GWIS. The country-profile downloads page is a JS app; grepping its _nuxt bundles revealed the base URL cprof.effis.emergency.copernicus.eu and paths /api/v3/aoi, /countries, /subcountries, /indicators, /banf, /emissions. /api/v3/countries?env=GWIS returned a JSON country list (e.g. {iso3:'AFG',continent_code:'UN_ASI'}). /api/v3/aoi?env=GWIS returned continents. /banf with guessed params returned 'Internal Server Error'. drilldown_paths: HEAT: world heatwave days per person 1986-2024, observed vs 'without climate change' (Lancet 1.1.1 attributable, Global sheet), then WHO region / HDI group, then country (Country sheet), then who is hurt: over-65s and infants (Lancet 1.1.1 vulnerable), heat deaths 1990-2021 (Lancet 1.1.5), and work hours lost by sector, e.g. agriculture and construction (Lancet 1.1.3), then a seasonal update ('1.5bn people got 30+ extra risky-heat days in Jun-Aug 2026', Climate Central CSI), then the future: heat at 1.5 vs 2.6°C (IPCC Atlas regional aggregates; CAT thermometer), then what you can do.

IS THIS CLIMATE CHANGE? Map of attribution studies (Carbon Brief CSV: 967 cases, filter by hazard type), then country, then event card with classification and a link to the paper, plus the latest WWA rapid study (WWA wp-json list) and its vulnerability findings, then the human toll for that event (IDMC event row: displacements; EM-DAT aggregate deaths, link-out only), then what made it deadly / what reduces risk (WWA vulnerability section).

DISASTERS AND DISPLACEMENT: global disaster displacements 2008-2025 by hazard (IDMC GIDD CSV), then country choropleth, then top events per year (event_name), then cross-link to attribution (Carbon Brief/WWA). For the U.S. branch: billion-dollar disasters per year by hazard, cost, deaths, by state (Climate Central; NOAA 1980-2024 archive as public-domain baseline), with a provenance note that NOAA retired the product and Climate Central continues it.

WILDFIRE: global burned area 2002-2025 (GWIS via OWID CSV), then continent, then country, then land cover (GWIS API), then this season's anomaly by country and biome (State of Wildfires Zenodo CSVs), then attribution callouts (Canada ~61x more likely burned area, NW Iberia ~3x fire weather; SoW 2025-26), then health from smoke (Lancet 1.2.1 person-days above the WHO PM2.5 guideline), then future burned area under SSP1-2.6 vs SSP3-7.0 (SoW).

DROUGHT AND FOOD: country SPEI-12 1901-2024 (SPEIbase v2.11 / LCSC country series), then drought years highlighted, then WWA drought attribution where available, then drought displacement (IDMC hazard_type 'Drought'), then crop impacts per °C (Hultgren et al. 2025; ISIMIP3b maize and wheat ensemble by warming level), then the 1.5 vs 2.6°C comparison.

OCEANS AND COASTS: coral reef heat stress map (NOAA CRW daily DHW), then the four global bleaching events (21% to 37% to 68% to 84% of reef area; NOAA statements), then sea-level rise to 2100 by scenario (IPCC AR6 Sea Level Projections, Zenodo), then a coastal location, then people living less than 1 m above sea level by country (Lancet 2.3.3).

WHERE ARE WE HEADING? CAT thermometer (2.6 / 2.2 / 1.9°C) and UNEP EGR 2025 (2.8; NDCs 2.3-2.5°C), then a warming-level slider (+1.5/2/3/4°C) driving IPCC Atlas regional changes in hot extremes and heavy rain, plus SPM.9 counts of regions where impact-drivers change at +2°C, plus sea-level and crop-yield panels, then the 'gap' (35%/55% cuts vs 2019 needed by 2035; UNEP), then action links.

EUROPE DEEP DIVE: heat-stress days and tropical nights 1950-2025 (ESOTC fig05.4 CSV), then the 2025 record wildfire season (SoW Europe; ESOTC wildfires), then heat deaths in Europe (ESOTC citing Lancet Countdown Europe), then WWA European heatwave attribution (26 Jun 2026).
research.action_links:
How each consequence connects to action (every claim should link to its source):
(1) Warming pathways are a choice. CAT shows 2.6°C under current policies vs 1.9°C if net-zero pledges are met (CAT COP30 xlsx). UNEP EGR 2025 quantifies the cuts needed: 35% (2°C) and 55% (1.5°C) below 2019 by 2035 (doi:10.59117/20.500.11822/48854). Each impact panel should therefore show both the 'current policies' and the 'pledges met' value side by side, using the IPCC Atlas, sea-level and SoW projections. For citizens and policymakers, link to CAT country pages (climateactiontracker.org/countries/) to compare their own government's rating against the gap.
(2) Heat is the deadliest and most attributable consequence (Lancet 1.1.5 and 1.1.1). Lancet Countdown's response indicators cover adaptation and health system preparedness, so link to lancetcountdown.org/explore-our-data/ sections 2.x. The WWA vulnerability sections of each heat study (worldweatherattribution.org) describe interventions such as heat action plans, early warnings and cooling access, so communities can see what reduced deaths.
(3) Disasters and displacement: IDMC GRID 2026 (doi:10.55363/IDMC.ETWG8973) documents pre-emptive evacuations, which save lives and inflate displacement counts. That is a lever for early warning. Link the 'what can be done' text on event cards to it.
(4) Wildfire: SoW 2025-26 shows burned area under SSP1-2.6 is 5-36% lower than under high emissions across focal regions (doi:10.5194/essd-2026-587). That is the mitigation link. Lancet 1.2.1 links smoke to health.
(5) Individual-level actions belong to the 'causes' domain (emissions by sector). From this domain, the user-facing bridge is: pick a consequence, see which warming level it scales with (IPCC Atlas), then see which emissions pathway gets there (CAT/UNEP), then follow a link to the causes and solutions pages.
Keep the tone factual. The site does not advocate specific policies; it shows sourced numbers and links to the producers' own recommendations.
research.gaps_and_risks:
LICENSING (most important for CSV downloads):
- Lancet Countdown is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Our derived CSVs must also be CC BY-NC-SA, and the site must stay non-commercial forever.
- Carbon Brief allows only unadapted, non-commercial reproduction (ND-like). Offer derived counts and link to their CSV; ask permission before redistributing a filtered CSV.
- EM-DAT prohibits distributing 'a substantial part', sharing 'any portion via the Internet to unauthorized users', and building derivative databases. Its export is registration-gated, and the FAIR archive is CC BY-NC-ND. Show aggregate charts only, offer no EM-DAT CSV downloads, keep no public mirror, and seek written permission from CRED. OWID's EM-DAT charts inherit EM-DAT terms; they are NOT CC BY.
- Climate Central's ToS bans bulk or automated download. Ask permission to automate ingestion of the billion-dollar database. Climate Matters articles themselves are CC BY 4.0.
- CAT requires credit to both organisations, a copyright notice, and no commercial use. UNEP allows non-profit reproduction with acknowledgement. WMO allows short extracts only. IPCC figures may not be altered (redraw from the CC BY 4.0 CEDA/Atlas data instead). WWA and Climate Impact Explorer have no formal licence. SPEIbase is ODbL (share-alike database).

STATUS AND US-FEDERAL RISK:
- NOAA retired Billion-Dollar Disasters in May 2025. The archive page still serves events-US-1980-2024.csv, but its total-cost sentence renders blank, a sign of no maintenance. Mirror it now with a SHA-256 hash.
- NOAA Coral Reef Watch is federally funded. Archive the event statistics and announcement text.
- The NASA AR6 sea-level projection tool URL (sealevel.nasa.gov/ipcc-ar6-sea-level-projection-tool) returned 404. Use Zenodo as primary.

FRAGILE ACCESS:
- unep.org and wedocs.unep.org sit behind a Cloudflare challenge (403 to scripts), so archive the PDF manually.
- The GWIS country-profile API is undocumented: the /banf parameters are unknown and the bulk ZIPs linked in its JS return 404.
- The Climate Impact Explorer API is legacy (RCP-era); its documented example returns 404.
- The IDMC website is client-rendered. Use the HDX copies, which IDMC publishes.
- Pipeline design: pin every number to a dated vintage plus a file hash, and fail loudly on schema change. Per owner rules, no heuristic fallbacks.

VINTAGE AND SCHEDULE:
- Lancet 2026 global report: 28 Oct 2026 (24 days away; plan an update).
- CAT COP31 update and UNEP EGR 2026: about Nov 2026.
- WMO SoGC 2026: about Mar 2027. IDMC GRID 2027: about May 2027. OWID EM-DAT: 2027-04-30. OWID GWIS: 2027-09-11.
- State of Wildfires 2025-26 is a preprint under review; values may change.
- SPEIbase ends Dec 2024. The LCSC country-SPEI zip dates from July 2024 (older version than v2.11).

METHODOLOGICAL CAVEATS TO SHOW IN UI:
- EM-DAT event counts rise mainly with reporting.
- Billion-dollar costs rise with exposure and wealth, and the CPI base year changes between releases.
- Attribution literature is geographically biased toward Europe, North America and East Asia.
- Heat mortality is modelled and stops at 2021.
- Displacements count movements, not unique people.
- MODIS-based burned area underestimates small fires. Continuity risk to the MODIS record as Terra/Aqua age is plausible but was not verified in this session.
- CSI and Lancet use different heat definitions; never combine them.

GAPS NOT FILLED:
- No openly licensed global economic-loss dataset (Munich Re NatCatSERVICE, Swiss Re sigma and Aon are proprietary; not fetched; treat as 'avoid'). EM-DAT damages are sparse.
- No open, structured WWA results table (needs hand curation with a quote per number).
- AR6 WGII impact figure data was not found on the CEDA badc filesystem (only WGI and SR1.5).
- Crop-yield impacts need offline processing of ISIMIP NetCDF.
- The Climate Central CSI country tables have no public machine-readable file.
- WebSearch budget was exhausted near the end, so Munich Re/Swiss Re terms and the latest NOAA CRW historical event percentages for 1998 and 2010 were not independently re-verified.

verification.domain: Consequences and impacts: health, heat, disasters and losses, displacement, wildfire, drought, coral reefs and sea level, crops, attribution of extremes, and projected warming outcomes. All checks below were run on 2026-10-04 with live curl and WebFetch requests. Files were parsed in memory only.

verdicts.name: Lancet Countdown 2025 global indicator data (1.1.5, 1.1.3, 1.1.1, 1.2.1, 2.3.3)
verdicts.corrections: I downloaded and parsed all 6 xlsx URLs (HTTP 200, real OOXML). The DATA GUIDANCE sheet and lancetcountdown.org/use-our-data/ both state CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The citation and DOI match Crossref: Lancet 406(10521):2804-2857, issued Dec 2025. The homepage confirms the 10th (2026) report launches on 28 October. Four fixes are needed in how the data is used. (a) The 1.1.1 'Attributable' workbook covers 2020-2024 only (Global sheet columns: Observed, Counterfactual, Attributable_to_CC). The drill-down path's '1986-2024 observed vs without climate change' chart cannot be built from it. The 1.1.1 'Vulnerable' workbook covers 1980-2024, but only exposure for infants and people aged 65+/75+. (b) 1.1.5 heat mortality has only Global, WHO, LC and HDI sheets. There is no country sheet. (c) 2.3.3 is a single cross-section: 163 country rows, one column 'population_exposed_1m_SLR (million)', no year column. The method is a bathtub model of cells inundated under 1 m of global mean sea-level rise (CoastalDEM), so it should not be described as a 2024 time series. (d) The guidance sheets say third-party inputs keep their own licences (e.g. ERA5, GPWv4, GBD 2021).

verdicts.name: IDMC Global Internal Displacement Database (GIDD) / GRID 2026
verdicts.corrections: LICENCE CONFLICT. HDX package_show does say license_id 'cc-by-igo'. But IDMC's own GIDD export disagrees. That export is https://helix-tools-api.idmcdb.org/external-api/gidd/displacements/displacement-export/?release_environment=RELEASE&start_year=2008&end_year=2025&client_id=..., which 302-redirects to an S3 xlsx. Its README sheet states 'USE LICENSE: This content is licensed under CC BY-NC. See: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/'. Treat the data as CC BY-NC 4.0, since the publisher's own statement is the stricter one. The same README gives 'LAST UPDATE: August 31, 2026', so the GIDD changed after the May release. It also says API keys must be requested from ch.datainfo@idmc.ch, so do not reuse the HDX client_id in our pipeline. IDMC's prescribed data citation is: 'Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre. Global Internal Displacement Database. IDMC (2026). Available at: https://www.internal-displacement.org/database/displacement-data/ (Accessed: [date])'. The HDX CSV has NO HXL tag row (header then data; 29,698 data rows), so 'CSV with HXL tags / skip the HXL row' is wrong. GRID 2026: PDF HTTP 200 (13.4 MB); Crossref published-print is 2026-05-12; the DOI 10.55363/IDMC.ETWG8973 and the p.3 citation are confirmed. The PDF itself contains no licence statement.

verdicts.name: U.S. Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters (Climate Central continuation)
verdicts.corrections: Confirmed: the landing page says 'As of June 2026... 438 such events... exceeding $3.2 trillion', with 17,377 deaths, CPI-adjusted to 2026 dollars. Confirmed: the /what-we-do/legal text (non-commercial use; credit plus a link required; 'Any bulk downloading is prohibited'; automated extraction is prohibited). Fixes: (1) The page says 'As of July 28, 2025, Climate Central manages and maintains this billion-dollar disaster dataset'. The first public release was October 2025, per the 2025-in-review page. 'Since Oct 2025' is therefore only the release date. (2) The CC BY 4.0 notice on Climate Matters pages covers text, graphics and multimedia only. The same block says 'Permission to use data and other materials published on this page is granted for non-commercial uses... as governed by Climate Central's Terms of Use'. So the 2025-in-review numbers are not CC BY data. (3) You cannot build 1980-2025 by adding 2025 to NOAA's archive. NOAA's 16,941 deaths + 276 = 17,217, but Climate Central reports 17,194, so Climate Central revised historical records.

verdicts.name: NOAA NCEI U.S. Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters (archived 1980-2024)
verdicts.corrections: The CSV returns HTTP 200 text/csv with 2 preamble lines and then the header. It has 403 events, a CPI-adjusted sum of $2,917.6B and 16,941 deaths. 2024 has 27 events, $182.7B and 568 deaths. The landing page carries the citation and DOI 10.25921/stkw-7w73 verbatim. No licence page was fetched; public-domain status rests on 17 USC 105 (US federal work). The advice to mirror the file with a SHA-256 hash is sound.

verdicts.name: EM-DAT: The International Disasters Database
verdicts.corrections: The terms-of-use prohibitions are quoted accurately (no distributing a substantial part, no derivative databases, no sharing any portion via the Internet to unauthorized users). Correction: the FAIR archive is not a '2024 archive'. Dataverse API for doi:10.14428/DVN/I0LTPH shows latestVersion 2, released 2026-04-30. Its files include 260430_emdat_archive.xlsx (8.1 MB) and 260430_emdat_columns.csv, both restricted=false, so they download without login. The licence is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (SPDX CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0). This gives a versioned, citable, registration-free pipeline input. ND still bars sharing adapted or derived datasets, so the 'aggregate charts only, no CSV downloads' policy still holds. A non-commercial mirror of the unaltered archive file would be permitted.

verdicts.name: Our World in Data mirrors (EM-DAT disasters, GWIS burned area)
verdicts.corrections: The metadata is confirmed. GWIS series: lastUpdated 2026-09-11, nextUpdate 2027-09-11, origin licence CC BY 4.0 (indicator 1306111). EM-DAT series: lastUpdated 2026-04-30; origin licence 'UCLouvain 2026', linking to the EM-DAT terms; EM-DAT datePublished 2026-04-28. The single 'open-attribution' label is wrong for this entry as a whole. Only the GWIS series is open-attribution. The EM-DAT-derived series stays under EM-DAT terms (restricted). Important data caveat: OWID's continent 'Europe' row of the GWIS series gives 7,554,890 ha for 2025. That is 49.6% BELOW its 2002-2024 mean and lower than 2024 (11.59 Mha). This directly contradicts a 'Europe record fire season' headline unless Europe is defined using EFFIS geography.

verdicts.name: Global Wildfire Information System (GWIS) country profiles
verdicts.corrections: The data-license page (HTTP 200) has the CC BY 4.0 wording as quoted. /api/v3/countries?env=GWIS returns JSON, e.g. {iso3:'AFG', continent_code:'UN_ASI'}. The S3 MCD64A1_burned_area_full_dataset ZIPs return 404 for both 2002_2024 and 2002_2025. The API is undocumented, as stated. No change needed.

verdicts.name: State of Wildfires 2025-26 (report preprint and Zenodo regional summaries)
verdicts.corrections: The Zenodo record 21262381 is confirmed: published 2026-07-22, cc-by-4.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21262381. It is the newest of 4 records in concept 10.5281/zenodo.11400539. Its version field is null, so 'v4' is not an official version label. It also holds files not listed by the researcher: SUPPLEMENT_VNP64A1 and SUPPLEMENT_MRBA60 burned-area CSVs, and Burned_Area_period_stats.csv. The preprint is confirmed: received 22 Jul 2026, discussion started 3 Aug 2026, CC BY 4.0, under review. Three corrections. (1) 19,629 km² for Europe is NOT a State of Wildfires result. The preprint quotes it as the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) estimate, '301% above the 2006-2024 average'. That is about 4x the average, not about 3x. The preprint also notes EFFIS coverage differs from its own definition of Europe. Cite EFFIS as the primary source. (2) '+78% by 2100 under SSP3-7.0' applies to the Northwest Iberia focal region (fires of the same return interval). It is not a global burned-area projection. (3) The confirmed statements are: Midwestern Canadian Shield burned area about 61x more likely; fire weather doubled in likelihood; NW Iberia fire weather about 3x more likely; Chile burned area about 36% larger; SSP1-2.6 reduces burned area by 5-36% across focal regions.

verdicts.name: Carbon Brief attribution map (papers-download.csv)

Licence: the footer's 'CC license' link points to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/legalcode. The licence is therefore explicitly CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, not merely 'effectively' so.
